question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{" separators="|"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>, then number of non-empty subsets <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> such that the product of elements in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is even is :

solution.text:
As we know that the product of numbers is even when at least one of the number must be even.

Hence total subsets of A in which product of numbers is even = Total subsets – total subsets in which all the elements are odd

=2100-250=250250-1.
